one_month_reasoning: The Oct 27-28 FOMC decision (announced Oct 28) falls inside the window, as do late-October peer prints (TI, NXP, STM). onsemi's own Q3 report is still unconfirmed and estimated for about Nov 2, just outside the window, with a small chance it lands earlier. The supervisor puts October hike odds at about 69% as of Sep 29. When I re-read DeFiRate, its snapshot (taken 2026-09-30 02:02 ET) showed 44% hike and 55% hold (Kalshi 44.5c, Polymarket 43.5c; 24-hour volume about $183k on Kalshi and $192k on Polymarket), after a 21-point drop over the week. The 69% figure looks like the level before that drop. Either way the market is split and the outcome is largely priced, so the FOMC adds variance rather than drift. The CFO's $8.2M sale is a mild negative. The ~14% rebound from the Sep 16 low of $65.80 works against the weak 3-month trend. With no directional edge, I use a symmetric lognormal on $75.95 with sigma of about 0.175, near annual realized vol / 3.5, nudged slightly up for the FOMC and the risk of an early earnings date.

fair_value.method: A 60/40 blend of forward P/E and FCF yield. P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of about $4.85 (a haircut CY27 of $4.20 rolled into a CY28 of $5.05, built from consensus growth instead of the Substack figure) x 16.5x = $80. FCF: normalised NTM FCF of $1.65B (capex at ~5% of revenue, not the Q2 trough of ~2%) / 395M shares = $4.18 x 18x = $75. The blend gives about $78.

ON trades at about 16.8x CY27 consensus today, and NTM EV/EBITDA is about 12x (TIKR). A 16.5x multiple assumes no rerating while the Fed is still hiking and prediction markets split on the October decision. The Substack 16-18x cyclical range is no longer used as a basis.

bear.story: Auto and China demand stays weak, the Chinese SiC price war squeezes device margins, and the Fed keeps hiking. CY27 EPS lands around $3.50, capex normalises and Synaptics integration drags, so the stock rerates to about 13.5x and retests the 52-week low of $44.56.

base.story: Gross margin moves into the low 40s as utilisation rises, AI data center revenue roughly doubles in 2027, and the Synaptics deal closes mid-2027 without surprises. NTM EPS of about $4.85 at 16.5x, with FCF held back by capex normalising toward 5% of sales.

bull.story: The AI power ramp and an auto/industrial recovery push CY27 EPS toward the top of the range (about $5.40) and CY28 toward BofA-style levels (about $6). Progress toward the 2030 targets rerates the stock to about 20x NTM, close to the mean street target of $104-118.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $52 the stock would trade at about 11.5x CY27 consensus EPS ($4.53) and a 7-8% yield on normalised FCF, levels seen only near cycle troughs. Getting there most likely requires a real earnings reset, not 50-60% vol noise: a Q4 guide cut, gross margin guided back below 38%, AI data center revenue failing to grow, a SiC impairment or price war reaching device margins, or a failed or renegotiated Synaptics deal.

reasoning: Round 2 changes are small and mostly downward. (1) As the supervisor asked, I dropped the paywalled single-author Substack CY28 EPS ($5.72) as an input and anchored CY28 on consensus growth. Alpha Vantage and stockanalysis confirm CY26 $3.20 and CY27 $4.53 (31 analysts, revised up from $4.31 over 90 days) but give no CY28 figure. Assuming +20% growth on my haircut CY27 gives $5.05, so NTM EPS falls from $4.90 to $4.85 and the P/E leg stays at about $80. (2) I accepted the supervisor's capex-trough finding: Q2 capex was $34.3M (~2% of sales) against a ~5% model. My round-1 $1.7B held FCF flat on the trough, and normalising capex while growing operating cash flow gives $1.65B, so the FCF leg falls from $78 to $75. Fair value moves from $80 to $78, about 3% above spot. (3) FOMC: I partly disagree with the supervisor. A fresh DeFiRate read (Sep 30 02:02 ET, about $375k of 24-hour volume across the two markets) still shows about 44% hike after a 21-point weekly drop. The 69% figure appears to be the pre-drop level. I accept the Oct 28 date and the conclusion that the meeting adds variance, not drift. The 1-month ladder stays a symmetric lognormal on spot with sigma of about 0.175. The 12-month ladder is a lognormal with median about $78 (from about $80) and sigma about 0.48, with slightly fattened tails. That is below the 64% realized vol, which the one-off June deal gap inflates, but well above a typical large-cap. Scenarios are $48 / $80 / $118 at 25/50/25 (mean about $81.5, above the median because of right skew). The thesis break stays at $52. The Workopia jobs signal was discounted by the supervisor and no longer carries weight. Research was limited: TheStreet, Simply Wall St and Benzinga pages returned 403, so the BofA CY28 figure comes from a search snippet and is used only as a cross-check.
